Young's 1803 description: small hole in a window-shutter, sunbeam (reflected in by a looking-glass), 'a slip of card, about one-thirtieth of an inch in breadth'; lecture read 24 November 1803
checks.note: Young used a mirror outside the shutter; 'let a thin beam of sunlight in' is a fair simplification.

checks.claim: Fringes in the card's shadow from light passing both sides; blocking one side made them disappear ('all the fringes which had before been observed in the shadow on the wall immediately disappeared')
checks.note: With sunlight Young saw coloured fringes; 'bright and dark bands' is a fair 9th-grade simplification (Grokipedia also says bright and dark fringes).

checks.claim: Key: in a dark band light from the two sides met crest on trough and cancelled (destructive interference)
Wrong: crest on crest and added (that makes the bright bands)
Wrong: particles colliding; card edges soaking up the light (blocking one side would not then remove the bands)
Context: the fringes told against Newton's corpuscular theory

Stem logic: inverted wave delayed a further half wave is back in phase, so crest meets crest and the drone is louder (whole-wave delay would still cancel, which is the distractor 'cancelled just as well')
checks.note: Holds for the steady drone treated as one wave, as the stem does; a real drone's even harmonics would behave differently, beyond grade level.
